analyzed_vuln.description: In `Compiler::simplifyExpression`, constructor-flattening uses a 32-bit `int argsToOptimize` bitmask and shifts `currBit <<= 1` once per constructor argument. For constructors with many arguments, `currBit` overflows/UB and tracked bits become invalid, so the second pass may treat non-constructor arguments as if they were constructors (`arg->as<Constructor>()`) and build malformed IR. This leaves expressions/types referencing poisoned pool memory, later crashing as a use-after-poison in `Type::columns()` when optimizer revisits the corrupted expression tree.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `FuzzSkRuntimeEffect` input, supply SkSL that produces a constructor expression (`float[]()` pattern in the PoC) with enough arguments/nesting to drive the flattening path in `simplifyExpression` (`c.type().columns() > 1`) and overflow the bitmask bookkeeping. During `scanCFG` optimization, the corrupted constructor-argument handling causes invalid expression/type references; a later `c.type().columns()` read hits poisoned memory and ASan reports UAP.
